intuition: Sort the numbers so equal values are together. Build subsets by choosing later positions. At one step, choosing either of two equal values would start the same family of subsets, so try only the first. A later step may still choose another copy to include duplicates in a subset.

Sort the values, then explore increasing indices. At one recursion depth, equal values are interchangeable next choices: only their first occurrence needs its own branch. At a deeper depth, another equal value is meaningful because it increases that value’s occurrence count in the current subset.

This explains the condition i>start rather than i>0. It skips equal siblings while preserving equal descendants. Save the path at every call, not only at leaves, because every partial selection is a valid subset, including the empty root path. Copy before future choices modify the shared path.

steps: For sorted nums=[1,2,2], visit the empty path first and save the empty subset.
Choose 1 and save [1]. Its first 2 produces [1,2], and the later 2 at the next depth produces [1,2,2].
Return to path [1]. Skip the second 2 as a sibling because the first 2 already represented that choice.
At the root, choose its first 2 and save [2]. The following equal 2 is now a descendant, so save [2,2].
Skip the root’s later 2 sibling. The result contains exactly six distinct subsets, with zero, one, or two copies of 2 as appropriate.

codeNotes.note: Each call represents a subset already chosen, regardless of whether more numbers will be added. Copying captures this exact intermediate selection.

concept.question: How can later equal copies remain useful while equal sibling choices disappear?
intuition: Equal occurrences can start identical families of subsets. Removing them entirely would lose subsets that need two copies, while exploring every equal sibling would duplicate results.

Sort the values. At any one selection step, try only the first of equal alternatives. Once a value is chosen, its later equal copy may still be chosen deeper in that path. Save each path, including empty.
concept.observation: Skip equal choices at the same depth, while permitting equal copies at deeper depths.
approach: Save the path and extend through later positions.
Skip equal sibling choices, then undo each extension.
concept.correctness: Every multiset subset can be built by taking its equal occurrences in sorted order. The earliest sibling choice permits all later copies as descendants, so it covers every needed multiplicity. Repeating a later equal sibling would cover the same family and is skipped. Every saved path therefore represents one distinct subset.

complexity.explanation: Worst-case output remains exponential when values are distinct. Sorting and the current path add linear-size working storage; copied subsets account for the output size.
